prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map places a large bent limb in the lower-right foreground, roughly 0.2–0.5 m from the camera, while the other person’s hand and forearm cross from the left at about 0.3–0.7 m and overlap that limb. The other person’s torso and helmeted head are farther ahead and left, approximately 0.8–1.5 m away; the ground and trench edge continue behind them at roughly 1–3+ m, with the small footwear near the upper-left farther than the people. Across the five frames, the foreground arm remains in contact or near-contact with the bent limb, while the other person shifts slightly left-to-right relative to the camera rather than clearly approaching or retreating. Depth makes the near arm–limb overlap and separation from the background clearer than RGB, but it is unreliable at silhouettes, in the dark upper background, and for converting relative brightness into exact metres.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map separates two person regions: a left-side figure that is partly outside the frame and a large foreground person region extending through the central arm and lower-right limb; their masks overlap where the hand rests across the limb. The left figure remains mainly in front-left of the camera, while the foreground limb stays within the camera wearer’s arm’s reach and the crossing hand is also within reach of both visible people. A blue region at the lower-right is labelled “banana,” although the RGB context does not support that identification and its shape changes sharply between frames, so it should not be treated as a reliable object location. The masks show occlusion boundaries that are difficult to follow in RGB, but they merge or split body regions inconsistently, omit the helmet, ground, footwear, and container-like object, and do not reliably indicate facing direction or distance.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is almost entirely empty in frames 1–4 and shows only a magenta hand skeleton in frame 5, located in the upper-right portion of that frame where the RGB shows a hand resting on the foreground limb. That hand is approximately 0.3–0.6 m from the camera and within arm’s reach, with its fingers directed generally rightward across the limb; no body skeleton is detected for the person ahead-left. Because the hand is the only tracked structure, the map cannot establish either person’s full posture, facing direction, gaze, inter-person distance, or approach and retreat across the sequence. It adds a rough finger-and-palm configuration that is hard to see in RGB, but the missing detections and compressed, distorted-looking hand geometry make it unreliable for broader spatial interpretation.
